reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    Jurisdiction: South Dakota
    Focus year: 2021

    Question: In an eviction action, can a tenant use their status as a victim of domestic violence
    as a rebuttal/defense?

    Statutes provided (only): SD Codified Laws  43-32-27 (2021) (retaliatory conduct cause of action).
*/

% ----------------------------
% Metadata (scenario context)
% ----------------------------
state(south_dakota).
focus_year(2021).

% ----------------------------
% Simple date arithmetic helper
% ----------------------------
% We model "dates" as integers representing days on a timeline.
days_between(Day1, Day2, Days) :-
    integer(Day1),
    integer(Day2),
    Days is abs(Day2 - Day1).

% ============================================================
% [1] SD Codified L  43-32-27 (2021) - Retaliatory conduct
% ============================================================

/*
  Citation: SD Codified Laws  43-32-27 (2021)

  A cause of action may arise for retaliation if, subsequent to a special event,
  the lessor:
    - increases rents above fair market value; OR
    - decreases electric/gas/water/sewer services; OR
    - gives notice to vacate when such notice is not based upon a breach of lease terms.

  Special events (after which retaliation is measured):
    (1) Lessor received written notice that lessee complained to code-enforcement agency
        about a building/housing code violation materially affecting health and safety,
        and the complaint is determined to be in good faith; OR
    (2) Lessee gave written notice to lessor of a condition requiring repair under  43-32-9; OR
    (3) Lessee organized or became a member of a tenant union/organization.

  Defense to the cause of action:
    It is a defense that the notice to vacate was given more than 180 days after the
    special event.

  Not retaliation:
    Failure of lessor to renew any written lease prior to or upon expiration is not retaliation.
*/

% --- Special events under  43-32-27 ---
statute_sdcl_43_32_27_special_event(code_complaint_good_faith).
statute_sdcl_43_32_27_special_event(repair_notice_under_43_32_9).
statute_sdcl_43_32_27_special_event(tenant_union_membership_or_organizing).

% --- Retaliatory acts under  43-32-27 ---
statute_sdcl_43_32_27_retaliatory_act(increase_rent_above_fair_market_value).
statute_sdcl_43_32_27_retaliatory_act(decrease_utility_services).
statute_sdcl_43_32_27_retaliatory_act(notice_to_vacate_not_based_on_breach).

% --- Express carveout: failure to renew written lease is not retaliation ( 43-32-27) ---
statute_sdcl_43_32_27_not_retaliation(failure_to_renew_written_lease).

% Determine whether a retaliation cause of action "may arise" on these abstracted inputs.
% Deterministic: succeeds once if the elements are met.
statute_sdcl_43_32_27_retaliation_cause_may_arise(Act, SpecialEvent, ActDay, EventDay) :-
    statute_sdcl_43_32_27_retaliatory_act(Act),
    statute_sdcl_43_32_27_special_event(SpecialEvent),
    integer(ActDay),
    integer(EventDay),
    ActDay >= EventDay,
    Act \= failure_to_renew_written_lease.

% Defense: notice to vacate given more than 180 days after special event ( 43-32-27).
% Deterministic: succeeds once if days difference > 180.
statute_sdcl_43_32_27_defense_notice_to_vacate_after_180_days(NoticeDay, EventDay) :-
    integer(NoticeDay),
    integer(EventDay),
    days_between(NoticeDay, EventDay, Days),
    Days > 180.

% ============================================================
% Scenario encoding (facts from the question)
% ============================================================

% Parties and case
eviction_action(case1).
tenant(case1, tenant1).
landlord(case1, landlord1).

% Key factual statement: tenant is a victim of domestic violence and wants to use that status as a defense.
tenant_victim_of_domestic_violence(tenant1).
tenant_asserts_defense(case1, domestic_violence_status).

% Helper predicate summarizing the scenario in logic form.
scenario_statement :-
    eviction_action(Case),
    tenant(Case, Tenant),
    tenant_victim_of_domestic_violence(Tenant),
    tenant_asserts_defense(Case, domestic_violence_status).

% ============================================================
% Reasoning layer: is DV status a defense/rebuttal in eviction?
% ============================================================

% We only treat something as a "DV defense available" if an encoded statute provides it.
% With only SDCL  43-32-27 provided, there is no DV-based eviction defense stated.
% This predicate is defined to avoid any undefined-predicate warnings.
statute_provides_domestic_violence_defense(_State, _Year) :-
    fail.

dv_status_is_a_recognized_eviction_defense_in_encoded_law :-
    state(State),
    focus_year(Year),
    statute_provides_domestic_violence_defense(State, Year).

% ============================================================
% Required answer predicate
% ============================================================
housing_answer(Result) :-
    (   scenario_statement,
        dv_status_is_a_recognized_eviction_defense_in_encoded_law
    ->  Result = yes, !
    ;   Result = no, !
    ).

% ============================================================
% Main entrypoint (required)
% ============================================================
main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: In an eviction action, can a tenant use their status as a victim of domestic violence as a rebuttal/defense?
